title: Foundations: Showtunes - The Complete Guide
summary: What Showtunes is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Showtunes songs: Showtunes are Broadway's songbook: character-driven songs that advance a plot, from 11-o'clock numbers to comedy patter songs. The best work on stage and on the radio.

History: Rodgers and Hammerstein's Oklahoma! (1943) set the integrated-musical template. Sondheim, Lloyd Webber, and Lin-Manuel Miranda (Hamilton, 2015) each reinvented the form.

How the songs work: Showtunes favors the keys of C, F, G, Bb, Eb. Common forms include The 11-o'clock number: the show's emotional peak; Patter songs: words at breakneck speed. Players should master belting: chest voice at full power first, then character acting through song. Pit-orchestra keys.
